title: How the Suicide Squad Built NASA's Space Center
description: In 1936, a group of student rocketeers nicknamed the Suicide Squad was kicked off campus for dangerous explosions. They moved to a dry riverbed and built what became NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

beats.text: Campus outcasts blew up a lab and built NASA's premier space center.
beats.visual: photograph of early rocket research group in Arroyo Seco, 1936

beats.text: In 1936, Frank Malina teamed up with rocketeers Jack Parsons and Edward Forman.
beats.visual: photograph of Frank Malina with early rocketry apparatus, 1936

beats.text: Their motor tests caused explosions, earning the group the campus nickname Suicide Squad.
beats.visual: photograph of early rocket motor test explosion at Caltech, 1936

beats.text: After blasting through a wall, the squad was banished to a dry riverbed called Arroyo Seco.
beats.visual: photograph of the rocket team setting up tests in Arroyo Seco wash, 1936

beats.text: Working outdoors, they built takeoff rockets for propeller aircraft, proposing the name Jet Propulsion Laboratory in 1943.
beats.visual: photograph of Ercoupe aircraft taking off with JATO rocket booster, 1941

beats.text: In 1958, JPL launched America's first satellite, Explorer 1, before transferring to the newly created NASA.
beats.visual: photograph of Juno I rocket launching Explorer 1 satellite, 1958

beats.text: That former riverbed camp went on to manage Voyager 1, the first human craft in interstellar space.
beats.visual: artist's concept of Voyager 1 entering interstellar space, 2012

beats.text: America's space program began with a campus explosion.
beats.visual: photograph of GALCIT rocket team in Arroyo Seco, 1936
